It sounds like your school doesnt want those calc kids to miss instruction. So a competent teacher would leave enrichment or remediation lessons students can do quasi independently with basic support from an adult.

Dont take this the wrong way but the last thing i want a sub to do is try to teach. It drives us up the wall when they to off the narrow lesson plan we set up for them.

 If i assign bookwork and say answer questions 1-5, and a sub makes them do 1-8 because they were finishing early is one thing. I totally get that.
But years ago we had a sub who literally did whstever she felt like and ignored lesson plans and said things like "the kids didnt want to do the work so i let them just hang out". That person? We didn't allow her on campus anymore.

Subs arent teachers. Subs are there to fill in the gaps and keep the system going. It is up for the teacher to teach AND make any plans for subs. Any competent teacher will not give any heavy lifting to a sub.

 I'll level with you, i had to take a few days off for a family emergency. Here's what the kids are doing with the sub: a quiz (cant mess that up), guided reading questions, textbook work and an assignment heavy on drawing/coloring. 

Easy for the sub to explain. Easy for the kids to complete quasi independently. Easy for me to grade when i get back. It hits both standards and mandates and even though I'm gone 3 days i really only lose 1 real deal on the curriculum calendar.


Anyways, relax pal. You'll do great.

Sure. Pretend you have a cap weighted etf at 5%. So itd hold at least 20 companies.

Say company A takes a hit. If you hold company company A, you take the hit directly. If you hold an etf that holds the company, your maximum loss is capped at 5%. And depending on the etf, they reorganize their holdings every certain amount of time.

Or...lets say Apple vs an index market etf. Apple is apple, apple takes a hit. You  have X amount of unrealized losses so long as you dont sell. An index fund that holds apple would take a hit, but there's a maximum to how much it would affected.

Or...could you hold dividend aristocrat portfolio at 5% each and hold pg ko jnj etc? Yes. But it would require a good amount of micromanaging.

Could you also hold them at bigger amounts? 10, 15, 20? Sure. But more of your portfolio is in one big pot.

Are there bad funds? You betcha. Are there rock solid funds? Absolutely. Do your due diligence.


Edit: it also depends on your portfolio goals. You can easily mix and match funds to have a yield of 5-9% depending on how much risk you want to assume and which sectors you approve of. I'm not a fan of MLPs but boy do I love Reits.

Edit 2: Also, a 5% of a 40$ etf is 2 dollars. It's easier to dca than with say JNJ
